exercises.q: Джон запер дверь ___ (подвал), чтобы Джессика не смогла выйти.
exercises.prompt: John locked the basement door so that Jessica couldn't get out.
exercises.why: The genitive case has four main uses: to denote possession ('Michael's car', meaning 'the car of Michael'), to denote number ('five apples'), in negative constructions ('there are no books'), and after several important prepositions ('without me'). The genitive case of Russian nouns is more frequently used and has many more functions than any other case in the Russian language. The genitive case is used to denote the possessor or owner which in English is rendered by the ending -'s (-s') or by the construction with the preposition of: *Книга студента.* — The student's book. *Автомобиль учителя.* — The teacher's car. The genitive denoting the possessor or owner answers the question чей?… — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0). From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 23.  ·  «The genitive case is used to denote the possessor or owner … A noun in the genitive case is sometimes used to qualify (modify) another noun.» — DLI, Lesson 23.
